title: Chow–Taylor conjecture on Latin wide Young diagrams
statement: A Young diagram $Y$ is **wide** if, for every subset $S$ of its rows, the diagram formed by $S$ dominates its conjugate; a filling of $Y$ is **Latin** if it assigns to each row the numbers $1,\ldots,a_i$ injectively and is also injective in every column. **Chow–Taylor's conjecture.** If a Young diagram $Y$ is wide, then it is Latin. This is the converse of the theorem that every Latin Young diagram is wide; the paper states that it proves a weaker dual version, so the converse remains the conjectural claim considered here.
source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, He Guo and Daniel Kotlar, “2-covers of wide Young diagrams”, arXiv:2311.17670 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17670

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).
